name: local_neck_cumulative_volume_confusion
mechanism: Pair the narrow lower walls of A with the narrow middle waist of E using four partial original side-contour styles. This targets the misconception that the narrowest local neck creates the highest half-volume level, favoring E. No waterline, new contour, dimension or fill is added.
primary_math_proof: A widens upwards, so its lower half contains less than half its full volume and the half-volume water level is above midheight. B has constant cross-section and reaches midheight. C and E have top/bottom symmetric profiles and reach midheight. D widens downwards, so half volume is below midheight. Thus A is uniquely highest. This is a qualitative profile argument; no exact pixel-derived volume is assumed.

marker_roles.role: A left lower wall: narrow lower portion whose cumulative capacity controls a high half-volume level.
E left middle waist: paired local narrow feature invites local-neck reasoning rather than cumulative volume.
A right lower wall: narrow lower portion whose cumulative capacity controls a high half-volume level.
E right middle waist: paired local narrow feature invites local-neck reasoning rather than cumulative volume.
